answer_text: South Dakota lets people sell some foods made at home without a license, including certain refrigerated baked goods, sauces and fermented foods after food safety training, but prepared meals are not among the foods the law lists. Food service establishments need a license from the state Department of Health.

points.text: South Dakota's food licensing law does not apply to people selling non-temperature-controlled food prepared at a residence, home-processed canned goods, baked goods prepared at a residence, or other home foods the law specifically authorizes.

Producers who complete approved food safety training may also sell non-heat-processed fermented foods, kuchen and baked goods needing temperature control such as cheesecake and cream pies, and sauces and pesto kept at or below 41°F, plus frozen fruit and produce kept at or below 0°F.
The law's list of authorized home foods does not include prepared meals.

sources.title: SDCL 34-18-35 Sale of homemade foods and food products
SDCL 34-18-36.1 Food safety training - Authorized sales

points.text: To be exempt from licensing, the food must be sold in the seller's physical presence at the seller's primary residence, a farmers market, a roadside stand or another temporary sale venue, and the seller or a household member must personally deliver it at the sale.

Labels must show the product name, producer's name, physical and mailing addresses, phone number, date made, ingredients, a keep refrigerated or frozen directive where required, and a disclaimer that the product was home-processed rather than made in a commercial kitchen.

Canned goods must have a pH of 4.6 or less or a water activity of .85 or less. Sellers either complete department-approved online food safety training every five years or keep a processing authority's written verification of each recipe.
State law makes it a misdemeanor to operate a food service establishment without a valid license issued by the Department of Health.

The department's licensing steps are an online application and fee, a plan review questionnaire sent to the regional advisor, a state on-site inspection, and approval before the license is issued. Catering businesses and bakeries go through the same process.

Thirty days before construction starts, a detailed floor plan of the food service kitchen goes to the regional advisor. Plans for facilities over 4,000 square feet must be stamped by an engineer or architect.

sources.title: SDCL 34-18-9 License required to operate lodging or food service establishment or campground

points.text: State rules (ARSD 44:02:07:03) require at least one person on a food service establishment's staff to have passed an 8-hour food service training and certification program.
The Department of Health says the certified food service manager requirement must be met before the on-site licensing inspection.
Business entities register with the Secretary of State online, or create the forms online and mail them in with an added $15 paper processing fee.

The state sales tax rate is 4.2%. Cities may add a municipal sales tax and a gross receipts tax on prepared food for immediate consumption, but the Department of Revenue says meals that require heating or baking are not subject to that gross receipts tax.
